blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In the UK, even disagreement is polite. You rarely hear "I don't agree." Instead, people say "I see your point, but…" or "I'm not sure I'd put it quite that way."

It can feel slow, but it has a purpose. It protects the other person. It keeps the conversation open. And it leaves room to change your mind without losing face.

The trick is simple. Say the soft words first. Only then say the real point — gently.

items.q: In the UK, what do people rarely say?
items.why: "You rarely hear 'I don't agree.'" — a discordância direta é evitada.

items.q: According to the text, why is polite disagreement useful?
options: It protects the other person and keeps the talk open
items.why: "It protects the other person. It keeps the conversation open."

items.q: What is the trick, according to the text?
options: Say the soft words first, the real point second
items.why: "Say the soft words first. Only then say the real point."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: Polite disagreement takes a little time
You can change your mind without losing face
Soft words help start a difficult talk
Being direct and blunt is the best way to disagree
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo defende a discordância suave, não a direta.

items.q: "I'm not sure I'd put it quite that way" suggests that the speaker…
options: does not agree, but says it gently
items.why: Inferência: é uma forma educada de dizer que não concorda.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientar uma analista júnior antes da reunião. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before the meeting, let's talk about how you disagree with James. His plan has a real problem, and you need to say so. But this is a British office, so please, be gentle.

Do not say "You are wrong" or "I don't agree." That sounds rude here, and people stop listening. Start soft. Say "I see your point, but…" or "I'm not sure I'd put it quite that way." Then, and only then, give your real point.

You can also say "Perhaps we could try a different date." The word "perhaps" opens a door. It does not close his idea. It just adds yours next to it.

Remember, this is not weakness. It is strategy. If you are soft first, James keeps listening, and you keep your influence. If you are hard, he stops. So breathe, say the kind words, and then make your point clearly. You will be fine.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie want the analyst to do in the meeting?
items.why: "His plan has a real problem, and you need to say so. But… be gentle."

items.q: Which words does Sophie tell her NOT to say?
items.why: "Do not say 'You are wrong' or 'I don't agree.'"

items.q: Why does Sophie like the word "perhaps"?
options: It opens a door and does not close his idea
items.why: "The word 'perhaps' opens a door. It does not close his idea."

items.q: Sophie says being soft is not weakness. She most likely means that…
options: soft words keep James listening, so you keep your influence
soft words make the meeting longer
you should always let James win
items.why: Inferência: "If you are soft first, James keeps listening, and you keep your influence."

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela tranquiliza a analista — "breathe… You will be fine."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "He was very polite in the meeting." Polite means…
items.why: Polite = educado, gentil e respeitoso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I want to ___ with the plan, but I will say it gently."
items.why: To disagree = discordar.

items.q: "Please tell her ___, so she does not feel hurt." Choose the word.
items.why: Gently = com delicadeza.

items.q: "I don't want to lose face in front of my boss." To lose face means to…
items.why: To lose face = perder a face, ficar constrangido diante dos outros.

items.q: "Her answer was indirect." Indirect means…
items.why: Indirect = indireto, não direto ao ponto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs úteis quando você discorda em uma reunião. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I see your point, but I'm not sure." To see someone's point means to…
items.why: See your point = entender o seu ponto, o que a pessoa quis dizer.

items.q: "She had to push back on the plan." To push back on something means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "The boss still has to sign off on the idea." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Perhaps we could try a different way." This is a polite way to…
items.why: É um modo suave de propor uma nova ideia sem fechar a do outro.

items.q: "They agreed but never followed through." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
